Definition: to cast together (stones), i.e. to lapidate
BiblicalUsage: Ragam is to cast stones together — to stone. Moses commanded that the one who gave his seed to Molech should be stoned with stones by the people of the land; Joshua stoned Achan with stones in the valley of Achor; and when Rehoboam sent Adoram to collect the tribute, all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that stoning was the congregation's judgment, not one man's anger: the whole people cast the stones, because the sin was against the whole people.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
